intro: On the hill above the Golden Horn rises a complex planned at the scale of a whole neighbourhood. You are at Süleymaniye Mosque, in İstanbul province, built between 1550–1557 by Sinan: mosque, colleges, hospital, baths and kitchens, all in one design.
history: This is Sinan's mature work, built for Süleyman the Magnificent between 1550 and 1557. The mosque was never meant to stand alone; it was designed as a piece of city, with four colleges, a medical school, a hospital, a soup kitchen, baths, a caravanserai and tombs. Even its walls hide a secret: hollow jars were set into them to serve the acoustics of the dome.
highlights: As you wander, look up first at the Main dome. Then don't miss the Tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem, the Colleges and the Hospital, and finally seek out Sinan's tomb.
facts: Did you know? Soot from the mosque's lamps was drawn by the airflow into a single chamber, where it was collected and made into ink for calligraphers. The hollow jars built into the walls work for the acoustics, so that without any amplification the imam is heard everywhere in the mosque. And Sinan placed his own tomb outside the complex, in a modest corner, facing not the mosque he built but the road leading to it.
outro: This brings our tour of Süleymaniye Mosque to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this place keep its calm for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
